large-counts.def: The check that the sampling distribution of $\hat{p}$ is approximately normal: at least 10 expected successes and 10 expected failures, $np \ge 10$ and $n(1 - p) \ge 10$ (some books use 5). It is never "$n \ge 30$" for proportions.

ten-percent.def: When sampling without replacement, the sample size is at most 10% of the population size. Then the selections are close to independent and the standard deviation formula for a statistic is accurate.

sd-phat.def: The spread of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion: $\sigma_{\hat{p}} = \sqrt{\frac{p(1 - p)}{n}}$, using the true proportion $p$. Four times the sample size halves it.
